entries.claim: Survivor.io's 2022-23 store screenshots each put one character in front with colour-coded CTAs and red accents on grey for action.
entries.appliesWhen: Store teardown of Survivor.io in January 2023; observation, not a test.

support.excerpt: Apptamin: each screenshot underlines a feature with one character in front and colour-coded CTAs; red stands out against grey backgrounds for action.

entries.useFor: Reference pattern for the closest survivor-like competitor; check the live page.
entries.researcherNote: Layout may have changed since 2023; no performance attribution.

entries.claim: Survivor.io's App Store first screenshot emphasised the challenge, the second showed build personalisation with weapon/skill combinations, and the third showed boss defeat.
entries.appliesWhen: Teardown, January 2023 (App Store, five screenshots).

support.excerpt: Apptamin: first screenshot emphasises the challenge, second highlights personalisation via weapon/skill combinations, third shows boss defeat mechanics.

entries.useFor: Sequencing benchmark: challenge, build, boss.
entries.researcherNote: Observation of one listing, one date.

entries.claim: Survivor.io used eight screenshots on Google Play against five on the App Store, with a landscape action-trailer video on Play and a portrait video on the App Store.
entries.appliesWhen: Teardown January 2023.

support.excerpt: Apptamin: App Store 5 screenshots, Play 8 (3 extra simple gameplay captures); Play video landscape, action-movie trailer style; App Store video portrait.

entries.useFor: Example of store-specific decks.

entries.claim: An analyst noted that Archero 2's store images focus almost only on core gameplay, which does not capture the 'Roguelike/Combat/Stage Experience 2.0' claims in the text.
entries.appliesWhen: Pre-launch teardown, 11 Nov 2024; one blogger's opinion.

support.excerpt: 'Habby has decided to focus more or less only on the core gameplay in the store images - which does not fully capture the strong statements in the text'.

entries.useFor: Habby's approach is gameplay-first imagery; differentiate with clearer promise text.

entries.claim: Archero 2 is a one-stick auto-attack roguelike with power-up choices, 50 main chapters, Sky Tower floors and a countdown survival mode.
entries.appliesWhen: Launch description; game facts not store imagery.

support.excerpt: Analyst: players stand still to auto-attack, defeat enemies, pick power-ups, beat bosses and survive timed objectives.
PocketGamer.biz: faster-paced combat, more skill control, a new countdown survival mode, 50 main chapters and 1,250 Sky Tower floors.

entries.useFor: Feature vocabulary for screenshot captions.

entries.claim: Habby's Archero 2 was estimated at about $27M per month and Capybara Go at about $19M per month in mid-2025.
entries.appliesWhen: Estimates reported August 2025; source of estimates not stated in the extract.

support.excerpt: Deconstructor of Fun: Archero 2 $27M/month (lifetime revenue per download over $11); Capybara Go $19M/month.

entries.useFor: Scale reference for competitor importance.
entries.researcherNote: Outside-in estimates; two of the five named competitors.

entries.claim: The original Archero earned about 31% of its revenue in the US, with South Korea and Japan the second and third most lucrative markets.
entries.appliesWhen: PocketGamer.biz, Oct 2024; original Archero lifetime spend over $350M.

support.excerpt: PocketGamer.biz: Archero generated over $350 million; the US accounts for 31%; South Korea and Japan are the second and third most-lucrative markets.

entries.useFor: Prioritise US, KR and JP creative for roguelike auto-shooters.

entries.claim: Capybara Go is a text-based roguelike adventure RPG with idle/auto-play combat, skill cards and animal companions.
entries.appliesWhen: Game description as reported at soft launch, September 2024.

support.excerpt: PocketGamer.biz: a 'text-based roguelike adventure RPG' where players outfit a capybara with skills, recruit animal companions and fight through randomised events.
Lancaric: text-based roguelike RPG with auto-play mechanics, resembling social casino games.

entries.useFor: Capybara Go blends the idle and roguelike genres Rogue Legend also straddles.

entries.claim: Capybara Go's UA creatives blend mass battles, survivor-style gameplay, UGC hooks and AI voiceover, with far more concepts in Asia than at the US launch.
entries.appliesWhen: Outside-in UA analysis, December 2024; concerns ads, not store images.

support.excerpt: Lancaric: creatives are 'the blend of every trend out there that works for mid-core'; only about 20% of Asian creative concepts were running in the US at launch.

entries.useFor: Hints that store visuals should echo the ad hooks that convert in Asia.
entries.researcherNote: Ad creatives, not store listings; author's estimates.

entries.claim: Capybara Go's top markets by revenue after global launch were South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, with the US fifth.
entries.appliesWhen: Outside-in estimate, December 2024.

support.excerpt: Lancaric: primary markets by revenue were South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, then (one unspecified), then the United States.

entries.useFor: Confirms KR, TW and JP as the priority creative markets for this genre.
entries.researcherNote: Estimate by a UA consultant; one market unspecified.

entries.claim: Legend of Mushroom earned about 69% of its first-months revenue in South Korea and Japan (39.4% and 30%), and both DoF and Sensor Tower report the two markets as its core.
entries.appliesWhen: To end of April 2024 ($270M global IAP per Sensor Tower); March 2024 split per DoF.

support.excerpt: Sensor Tower: $270M global IAP by end of April 2024; South Korea 39.4% ($106.2M), Japan 30% ($81M).
Deconstructor of Fun: in March Japan and South Korea were 'more than 2/3rds of total revenue' despite 'less than 20%' of installs.

entries.useFor: For an idle RPG, Japan and Korea drive revenue: weight creative testing toward them.
entries.researcherNote: Two independent market-data origins (Sensor Tower estimates, DoF).

entries.claim: Legend of Mushroom's user base in South Korea and Japan was over 80% male.

facts.of: Legend of Mushroom users in KR and JP

entries.appliesWhen: Sensor Tower, July 2024 APAC report.

support.excerpt: Sensor Tower: the user base is predominantly male, over 80% in South Korea and Japan.

entries.useFor: Audience assumption for competitor-pattern analysis.

entries.claim: Legend of Mushroom is an idle/slot hybrid: an ultra-simple idle gear-collection loop with gacha pulls up front.
entries.appliesWhen: Design analyses April 2024.

support.excerpt: DoF: an 'ultra-simplistic idle gear collection and enhancement loop' that resembles an 'RPG-themed slot machine'.
Naavik: 'a type of idle/slot hybrid' with gacha pulls front and center.

entries.useFor: Explains why gear-drop and power-jump visuals appear in the genre's creatives.

entries.claim: Legend of Mushroom is a fast-follow to Legend of Slime in theme and visuals, with casual visual styles and one-button gameplay.
entries.appliesWhen: Naavik digest.

support.excerpt: Naavik: 'an obvious fast-follow to Legend of Slime in terms of theme and visuals'; casual visual styles and one-button gameplay with deep monetisation.

entries.useFor: Competitor icons/screens in this niche look alike; distinctiveness is a risk.

entries.claim: Survivor.io reskinned Vampire Survivors' movement-only loop in a casual art style with meta-progression and peaked at about 25M MAU, earning over $120M a year.
entries.appliesWhen: Robin Guo essay, April 2024, quoting Sensor Tower.

support.excerpt: Peaked at ~25M MAU after launch and still generates $120M+ in revenue annually; casual art style plus battlepasses, piggy banks, crafting and lootboxes.

entries.useFor: Genre context for survivor-like positioning.

entries.claim: RPGs made up over 40% of mobile gaming in Japan and South Korea, with Japan preferring puzzle RPG and Korea action RPG/MMORPG (2020 data).

facts.of: RPG share in JP and KR

entries.appliesWhen: GameRefinery genre report, September 2020; may be outdated.

support.excerpt: GameRefinery: RPGs account for over 40% of mobile gaming in Japan and South Korea; Japanese players prefer Puzzle RPG, Koreans Action RPG/MMORPG.

entries.useFor: Why RPG creative matters in JP/KR; verify with current data.

entries.claim: Advisers recommend RPG and midcore creative built on character progression, boss encounters, world-building and character reveals, not feature lists.
entries.appliesWhen: Advice from AppFollow and ASOMobile; no conversion tests.

support.excerpt: AppFollow: screenshots showing character progression, boss encounters and social gameplay tend to outperform feature explanations.
AppFollow: RPGs should lean into world-building, character reveals and progression.
ASOMobile: RPG pages such as Genshin use cinematic stills and character art with a cinematic opener and character reveals.

entries.useFor: Rogue Legend RPG framing: character build and boss moments in frames 1-3.

entries.claim: In AppFollow's live audits, idle games were criticised for gameplay shown without captions, busy stylised frames, and portrait gameplay set in landscape frames with blurred backgrounds.
entries.appliesWhen: Expert opinion on CyberStrike Manager Idle and Idle Pirate Tycoon; not tests.

support.excerpt: AppFollow: 'Gameplay alone asks the player to work out what the game is'; Idle Pirate Tycoon's iOS gallery is portrait gameplay set inside landscape frames with blurred backgrounds.

entries.useFor: Add captions that explain the idle loop; consider the portrait-in-landscape frame pattern.

entries.claim: For casual and puzzle games, advisers say the first frame should show interaction fast, and Playrix uses artistic interpretations rather than raw gameplay.
entries.appliesWhen: Advice plus a Udonis observation of Playrix listings.

support.excerpt: AppFollow: puzzle/casual games should show the gameplay loop immediately and reveal interaction fast.
Udonis: Playrix uses artistic interpretations of gameplay across Homescapes, Gardenscapes and Fishdom.

entries.useFor: Do not copy the artistic-interpretation approach on Play.
entries.researcherNote: Observation and advice; conflicts with Google's requirement that screenshots show the actual experience.

entries.claim: GameRefinery reports Vampire Survivors-style survivor minigames being embedded in other mobile games such as State of Survival and Diablo Immortal.
entries.appliesWhen: GameRefinery trend article, 2024.

support.excerpt: GameRefinery: games like State of Survival and Diablo: Immortal incorporate 'Vampire Survivors-like minigames' where the character fires automatically.

entries.useFor: Shows the survivor-like mechanic is now common across genres.
